title: Value of the client_secret form parameter beside org_id in an Adobe Enterprise Web App token request
summary: A synthetic value of client_secret beside client_id, scope and the customer org_id in a raw form-encoded POST body, a curl -d argument and a curl --data-urlencode argument.
rationale: Adobe documents that the Enterprise Web App credential's backend sends client_secret as a form parameter with grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, scope and the customer org_id (contract claim enterprise-web-app-client-secret-request-parameter). Adobe states no prefix, alphabet, length or checksum, so the value is flagged because of the parameter it sits in. The extent is the value only. The client_id is the credential's public identifier; whether org_id is non-secret is not stated by the pages read, so it is not asserted either way and sits outside the span only because it is a different parameter.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, redact-secret#1228 Group C). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: a value in the client_secret form parameter of an Enterprise Web App token request is treated as a credential whatever its shape. Adobe documents client_secret as a form parameter of the Enterprise Web App token request (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and a generic attribution are the project's decisions. No subtype is inferred, and no prefix, width or alphabet is claimed.

sources.supports: The generate-access-token cURL request posts grant_type=client_credentials, client_id, client_secret, scope and org_id as form data, with placeholders for each; the sample response has access_token and expires_in.

The org_id is extracted from the id_token org_id claim and used with client_id, client_secret and scopes to generate access tokens; no refresh tokens are generated because the partner app can use client_id, client_secret, scope and org_id at any time.
sources.locator: sections "Step 3: Generating access tokens after the admin consents" and "Refreshing access tokens"

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
